elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Amended 11.1 retains a Customer-payable "Termination for Convenience Fee" and rewritten 13.5 expressly deems it "the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer," so a Customer-payable liquidated amount survives rather than being eliminated.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: 13.5 as rendered: "The Termination for Convenience Fee is Customer's sole early termination fee and is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement. No other amount payable by Customer under this Agreement shall be deemed liquidated damages or a penalty." The separate remaining-value "Termination for Cause Fee" is deleted from 11.2(A), which now applies the same single fee; residual Customer payments in 11.1/11.2(A) (unamortized Conversion costs, reasonable Expenses) are actual-cost reimbursements, not liquidated amounts, and are expressly excluded from liquidated-damages characterisation by 13.5.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: 11.1: "an early termination fee (\"Termination for Convenience Fee\") in an amount not to exceed three (3) months of Fees" — the REDACTED percentage of Estimated Remaining Value is removed and the cap is exactly at, not above, the three-month threshold; 11.2(A) now applies that same capped fee.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: 13.5 states the fee "is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement" and that no other Customer-payable amount shall be deemed liquidated damages or a penalty; no competing formula, instalment penalty or contingent LD mechanic remains (the instalment split in 11.1 merely times payment of the single capped fee).

reasons: Fallback level is complete: a single Customer-payable early-termination fee, expressly capped at three (3) months of Fees, and expressly stated in 13.5 to be the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.

Preferred level is not met and would require deletion of the fee entirely (and of the 13.5 liquidated-damages characterisation); the drafter correctly cures at the fallback, so the deviation is resolved to an acceptable position.

Edits are confined to the LD mechanics: the remaining-value percentage in 11.1 is replaced with the three-month cap; the separate Termination for Cause Fee (and its now-orphaned 13.4 carve-out sentence) is deleted from 11.2(A) because the defined term ceases to exist; 13.5's acknowledgement language is replaced because it was the operative provision deeming the fees liquidated damages. Removing "an Event of Default on the part of Customer" from the 11.1 applicability sentence is a necessary conforming change to avoid a retained sentence contradicting amended 11.2(A).

Retained favourable and unrelated mechanics survive: one-year notice, the 50/50 instalment timing, the Section 11.3 carve-out, Expenses/unamortized-cost reimbursement, and the pre-existing 13.4 exclusion in 11.1 (which is now harmless given the three-month cap).

Minor redundancy to tighten if convenient: the added phrase "and shall also apply as provided in Section 11.2(A)" in 11.1 is arguably surplus once the Customer-default carve-out is removed and 11.2(A) itself imposes the fee; it is a cross-reference for internal consistency rather than a new obligation, so it does not defeat minimality.

Verification caution the drafter should close: confirm no other section of the Agreement (e.g., schedules, exhibits, or a definitions article) still refers to the now-deleted "Termination for Cause Fee" or to "Estimated Remaining Value" solely for that fee, to avoid a dangling defined term; and confirm "Fees" is a defined term so the cap has a fixed base.
Non-checklist commercial point correctly flagged only in the rationale: the capped fee still triggers on any Customer Event of Default without a materiality or cure qualifier.
